newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Gold - Traders watch dollar, ignore German news.
newsitem.headline: Asian Gold - Traders watch dollar, ignore German news.

text.p: Asian gold took in its stride German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's comments that he wants Bundesbank gold reserves re-evaluated and focused instead on the weak dollar, bullion traders said on Friday.
"(Waigel's comment) just shows that central banks are re-evaluating their reserves," said one senior precious metals dealer, noting that Asian markets had not reacted to the news.

Waigel said on Thursday he wanted the Bundesbank's gold and currency reserves revalued from current low book prices to levels close to the normal market price after Bonn announced an 18 billion mark (US$10.6 billion) tax revenue shortfall, threatening Germany's prospects of qualifying for European monetary union (EMU).
Waigel said no Bundesbank gold reserves would be sold.

Hong Kong and Singapore bullion traders said the dollar's fluctuations, particularly against the yen, would continue to be a more important consideration as currency bounces had fuelled significant gold activity from Japan this week.
"I think they're looking to what the Japanese have taken up and whether they have filled themselves up (with gold)," said one Hong Kong dealer.
Singapore traders said the dollar's weakness may lend support to gold, with ample producer selling seen from Australia.
On Tokyo noon, the dollar was quoted at 116.69-72 yen after climbing as high as 117.06 yen in mid-morning.
Hong Kong gold was quoted at US$346.50/347.00 an ounce at 0400 GMT, up from its opening of $346.30/80 on buying from Japan.

"This week, with the fluctuating dollar/yen, the general public bought a lot on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) and trading houses in Japan tried to buy a lot on the spot market, so gold went up," a Hong Kong dealer at an international house said.
Some dealers reported healthy buying in Hong Kong of tael gold on Friday, possibly to accumulate interest on the gold exchange over the weekend.
"It looks like there is some physical buying at $346.50 per ounce and we should see the price hold at that level, provided the dollar/yen remains steady," another senior Hong Kong dealer said.
Bullion traders in Hong Kong and Singapore saw gold testing $350 again, with the weak dollar lending support to metals, including gold.

"There's good support at $346 to $347 (an ounce). But I think it will eventually challenge $350-$355," a Singpore source said. Another noted that the weak dollar had prompted speculative Far East buying.
Earlier this week, physical gold demand in most of Asia had dried up after prices marched to within sight of $350 an ounce, Singapore dealers said.
Singapore premiums over spot London prices were steady at 80-100 U.S. cents an ounce.
One dealer predicted the premiums may slip soon.
"It should move another 10 cents down. People are trying to keep it steady, but I think it will go much lower because of weak demand," the dealer said.
